_comment: FOR THE CUSTOMER, not applied by this repo.
The permissions policy for the role named in hosted-zones.json under
roles.cert_manager. Templated from a working deployment, so this is what
the role actually needs rather than a guess.
Its trust policy is the separate example-cert-manager-trust-statement.json,
which lets EKSManagerLetsEncryptRole in the shared services account assume
it.
Replace PUBLIC_ZONE_ID with the hosted zone id of the PUBLIC zone for this
environment. DNS-01 is validated over the public internet, so the
challenge record has to be written where Let's Encrypt can resolve it.
This is the tightest role in the system, and worth keeping that way. Every
statement is scoped as far as Route 53 allows:
ResolveZoneId            ListHostedZonesByName takes no resource, so it
is unavoidably on '*'. It reveals zone names,
not records.
ReadPublicZoneRecords    scoped to the one zone.
WriteAcmeChallengeRecords scoped to the one zone AND to TXT records named
_acme-challenge.* -- so a role that leaked could
not be used to repoint a hostname.
PollChangePropagation    GetChange is scoped to change/* rather than '*'.
Permissions on this role are your decision. This pair is known to work.
